name: Drowningman
label: Revelation
lede: Drowningman started in a Burlington, Vermont basement, went through at least 19 members in ten years, and blew up a tape machine making Rock and Roll Killing Machine. Its way out of a label deal was an album so bad nobody would release it.

eras.title: A basement on Hungerford Terrace
eras.text: Burlington had a real heavy-music scene in the mid-'90s, but Drowningman never quite belonged to it. The band took cues from Deadguy and Unbroken as much as Sunny Day Real Estate, and played Boston and upstate New York more than Vermont.

years.h: Simon Brody and four friends start Drowningman in Burlington
years.p: Denny Donovan, Javin Leonard, Dave Barnett and Todd Tomlinson complete the line-up. Some of them had played in a Boston emo band before.

years.big: "We didn't really belong to a scene. We still don't."
years.h: Drowningman plays its first show in a Hungerford Terrace basement
years.p: Brody on a band that played its first show on New Year's Eve in Burlington and was on tour almost at once.
years.xp:
The full line from Brody's No Echo interview: "We like to operate on the periphery." Vermont made that easy, since the nearest real circuit was Boston.

Seven Days describes a band that borrowed from metal's precision, prog's invention and old hardcore fury, and that Brody says wanted to "take a few things, mix them together and see what works."

years.h: Hydra Head, Converge's label, signs Drowningman and presses a 7"
years.p: Weighted and Weighed Down is the first record, on the Boston label that is home to [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]. Denny Donovan leaves the same year.

eras.title: Hydra Head takes a chance
eras.text: Hydra Head's Aaron Turner wasn't sure Drowningman could deliver an album after losing a key songwriter. They made it in Vermont, and Steve Evetts' mix changed how they heard themselves.

years.h: Busy Signal at the Suicide Hotline lands with a label that had doubts
years.p: Recorded in Vermont and mixed by Steve Evetts. Hydra Head's Aaron Turner had worried the band couldn't finish after losing a key songwriter.
years.xp:
Brody told No Echo the band picked Evetts for his work with Deadguy and Lifetime, with Turner's full support. The mix was done at Trax East, and two hours in Brody was astounded by what he was hearing.

Turner, doubtful at the start, was enthusiastic about the finished record.

years.h: A split 7" with The Dillinger Escape Plan, from New Jersey
years.p: Hydra Head pairs Drowningman with [[The Dillinger Escape Plan|1bc41dff-5397-4c53-bb50-469d2c277197]]. Guitarist Matt Roy joins the same year.

eras.title: The record that blew up the tape machine
eras.text: Drowningman moved to Revelation and made Rock and Roll Killing Machine through a week of broken gear and cabin fever. The release went badly, the relationship went worse, and the band answered with a joke album and a breakup.

years.h: Revelation's first Drowningman release comes in red, then pink
years.p: How They Light Cigarettes in Prison is REV 89: 220 copies on red vinyl, then 330 on pink.

years.big: "We just wanted to fucking kill each other."
years.h: A spike through the van floor starts the Killing Machine sessions
years.p: A metal spike through the van floor made Drowningman miss day one. The tape machine's wheel wobbled, the replacement part was wrong, and Brody says they waited from Monday to Friday without recording.
years.xp:
In Brody's telling to Exclaim!, the days went to Tony Hawk on PlayStation, no showers and the same restaurant every meal. At a second studio, with two songs of drums left, the tape machine started pouring smoke and blew up. The record was finished at a third place. Exclaim! lists Brian McTernan as producer.

Brody: "It was definitely a unique recording experience that will never be duplicated, hopefully. But I think it made the record what it is."

years.h: Rock and Roll Killing Machine comes out as REV 96
years.p: Simon Brody, Javin Leonard, Matt Roy, Dave Barnett and Joe Villemaire made it, and Terrorizer gave it 10 out of 10. The first vinyl run is 300 red and 1,350 black.

years.h: Drowningman steps outside Revelation for Equal Vision
years.p: Drowningman Still Loves You comes out as a 10" and a CD. In these years the band tours with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], The Dillinger Escape Plan and [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]].

yt: Brody on the unreleased LP, 2023 interview
years.h: Drowningman records Best Record Ever, badly, on purpose
years.p: To get out of its Revelation deal, the band cuts a deliberately terrible album at [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]]'s GodCity studio in Massachusetts. Revelation passes, and it's never released.
years.xp:
The trouble started with Revelation's handling of Rock and Roll Killing Machine. Brody told Louder that Papa Roach asked the band on tour, "but our label would have to rent the bus - they didn't pony up for it."

Ballou produced and played saxophone, soloed over 12-bar blues and pitched a track called Guitar Center Duel, two players mangling Sweet Emotion and Stairway to Heaven in separate speakers. [[Cave In|f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05]]'s [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] covered Ziggy Stardust with new words about Brody, with Converge's [[Ben Koller|b6fdd346-b9e8-449a-9105-612d3722503f]] on drums. Brodsky says Ballou told him, "This is too good, man!"

The band played it for Revelation's A&R person from the van, on tour. Brody: "They did not care for it."

years.p: The band breaks up after the set. Louder puts the end in summer 2002, after the label turned down its last record.

eras.title: Same name, new crew, a few shows
eras.text: Simon Brody and Denny Donovan revived the name with a new line-up and a big-bill tour. It fell apart within a week.

years.h: Learn to Let It Go: The Demos digs up the early tapes
years.p: Law of Inertia puts out the demos while Brody and Donovan put a new line-up together.

years.h: Thorp Records releases Don't Push Us When We're Hot
years.p: It's the third album, with Hans Olson, Jamie Durivage and Brian Curry alongside Brody and Donovan.

years.cap: Drowningman at Shorewood Legion Hall, Milwaukee, June 6, 2005
years.h: Three or four shows in, Drowningman quits again
years.p: The tour is badly organized, with The Dillinger Escape Plan, [[Misery Signals|0b0b523f-e9d5-4f18-919c-ebf084a58c26]], [[Every Time I Die|ef90f210-f136-4386-ab37-8c00d04eeace]] and Zao on the bill. The disgruntled band breaks up for a second time.
years.xp: Guitarist Frank Smecker and drummer Dave Joyal had rejoined for the tour. Seven Days counts at least 19 musicians through Drowningman between 1995 and 2005.

eras.title: The Killing Machine line-up, once more
eras.text: The Rock and Roll Killing Machine line-up played three Northeast shows, including a homecoming in Burlington.

years.h: Burlington gets the classic line-up back for $8
years.p: Brody, Leonard, Roy, Barnett and Villemaire play Signal Kitchen, one of three Northeast reunion shows.
years.xp:
Seven Days has it as a Friday, doors for a 7:30 p.m. show, 18 and over, with Surrounded By Teeth, As We Were and Zero Circle on the bill. Brody called it "the classic lineup," the one from the 2000 Revelation album.

By then Brody had become a lawyer based in Kansas.

eras.title: New songs, then "all theater"
eras.text: Drowningman came back with new songs as well as old ones, and Iodine Recordings reissued the debut. Then Simon Brody announced he was leaving, called the statement theater, and put the band on indefinite hiatus.

yt: Full set, Knitting Factory, Brooklyn, June 24, 2022
years.h: Sixteen years after the last album, the Later Day Saints EP
years.p: With guitarist Teej Maynard alongside Simon Brody, Javin Leonard and Matt Roy, Drowningman put the EP out on Iodine Recordings.

yt: hate5six, Decibel Metal & Beer Fest, April 15, 2023
years.h: Iodine puts Busy Signal back on vinyl
years.p: Iodine Recordings reissues the 1998 debut, remastered by Jack Shirley, with two bonus tracks.
years.xp: The bonus tracks are My First Restraining Order and Like Taking out Stitches with a Fork. Streaming came first, on May 24, with vinyl following in early 2023.

years.h: Brody's exit is "all theater," and Drowningman goes on hiatus
years.p: Brody's first statement also cited a contentious divorce, and he later called it all theater. On August 1 the band announces an extended, indefinite hiatus so he can focus on work, family and writing.
years.xp: Metal Injection's write-up ends on a shrug: it asks whether the hiatus is theater too, and answers, "Who the hell knows."
